A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DexGarmentLab environment, automated data collection pipeline and HALO policy. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and matchable despite renumbering and removal of v1's checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on 14 simulation tasks and four real-world tasks, including component ablations and baseline comparisons in Tables 2–3.

after.justification: v3 retains these results and adds policy transfer experiments, collection measurements, training-data comparisons and additional baseline evaluations in Tables 4–7.

M1.justification: Sections 4–5 retain GAM correspondence learning, demonstration retargeting and SADP's architecture and conditioning. The expanded LeapMotion discussion documents pose selection and reuse without establishing an algorithmic revision. Added transfer and training-data experiments use the existing policy.

E1.justification: The ClothesNet assets, 15-task environment, 14 evaluated simulation tasks and original four real-world tasks remain. Section 6.3.2 adds real-world Hang Trousers coverage and a policy-transfer scenario for Hang Trousers and Wear Hat using matched simulation and physical robot hardware.

E2.justification: Beyond retained DP and DP3 comparisons, Table 7 adds ACT, pi0 and RDT on four simulation tasks and real-world Fold Tops. Eureka adds numerical comparisons on Hang Coat and Wear Bowlhat; its remaining entries are unreported. This substantially broadens the evaluated comparator families.

E3.justification: v3 adds simulation-only versus simulation-plus-15-real-world-example training, automated versus teleoperated data controls, and pooled simulation/real-world data for VLA fine-tuning. It also identifies the retained real-world results as trained on real data, revising v1 Appendix F.3's blanket simulation-only training statement. This reporting revision does not establish that the unchanged original results were rerun.

E4.justification: The GAM/SADP ablations remain. New analyses test whether automated demonstrations match teleoperation data quality on three tasks (Table 6), whether real-world training examples mitigate transfer degradation on two tasks (Table 4), and how reliably and quickly the collection pipeline produces demonstrations (Table 5).

E5.justification: Both versions specify 50-episode simulation evaluations with three seeds and mean ± standard deviation, plus successful-trial counts for real-world evaluation. The added comparisons follow these reporting practices without introducing new uncertainty estimators, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 retain their original values. New Table 4 reports simulation-only transfer success of 8/15 for Hang Trousers and 9/15 for Wear Hat, versus 13/15 each with added real-world data. Tables 5–7 add collection outcomes, teleoperation-trained results and new baseline scores. Section 6.1 also revises the reported collection-time range from 30–60 to 30–80 seconds.

T1.justification: Appendix A retains the same adhesion and Coulomb-friction equations and associated definitions. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: a dexterous garment environment, automated collection from one demonstration, and generalizable hierarchical manipulation. The additional experiments support these existing claims without materially redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v3 distinguishes collection-pipeline transfer from policy transfer and discusses sensor noise, simulation gaps and baseline failure mechanisms. It replaces the missing-teleoperation-comparison limitation with explicit failures involving occlusion, severe deformation and unusual garment geometry (Appendix I.3). Appendix C also expands arguments about dexterous hands versus parallel grippers.

D1.justification: v3 documents manual filtering and reuse of LeapMotion poses, teleoperation devices, 50 demonstrations per real-world task, and the additional hardware and camera setup. Existing GAM/SADP training hyperparameters and compute details remain unchanged. Removing the checklist also removes the explicit repository URL, while the project link and release statements remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds Bathe's finite-element-method reference and Müller et al.'s position-based-dynamics reference. Appendix G extends comparisons and positioning to VLA and RL approaches, while Section 2's related-work discussion and principal novelty framing remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 divides the real-world section into two transfer routes, expands the LeapMotion explanation, inserts appendix sections C, F and G, and removes the NeurIPS checklist. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands result presentation through a new transfer-experiment Figure 10 and Tables 4–7 covering transfer, collection efficiency, data sources and broader baselines. Existing environment and physics figures are reordered, and Table 3 is relocated; the original method diagrams and task illustrations are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses v1's explicit lack of a teleoperation-data comparison and separately tests policy-level sim-to-real transfer, while broadening baselines and stating concrete policy failure conditions. These changes substantially strengthen validation and clarify what the real-world evidence establishes. Limited experiment sizes and new reporting errors, such as Table 5's 96.2% paired with 50/51, temper confidence but do not outweigh these gains.
